description: FFX Compatibility Tool 0.2.2 is a settings-page overhaul — the four panels are rebuilt on one shared row system under a search box that jumps to any setting, the theme controls become a segmented Light / Dark / System picker with a live preview, storage reads as a real disk meter with in-place delete confirms, and the About panel grows a proper update status card and an earlier-releases timeline.

changelog.title: ✨ What's New
items: A settings search that jumps — type in the box at the top of Settings and pick a match: the app switches to the right panel and flashes the row you asked for. Eighteen rows are indexed across Appearance, Storage, Plugin Profiles and About, so "logs", "palette" or "version" all land somewhere useful.

One shared row system — every setting now sits in the same rounded row (icon tile, title, caption, control on the right) with a hover state, grouped under small uppercase headers inside each card: Theme, Palette, Preview, Disk usage, Maintenance, What's new, Project, Updates.

The theme controls grow up — the dark-mode switch and the follow-the-Windows-theme checkbox become one three-way Light / Dark / System segmented control, the chosen palette swatch shows a checkmark with a small spring, a live preview card re-renders as you pick, and Restore Defaults is now a real two-step button that tells you what it did instead of a silent surprise.

Storage tells the truth at a glance — a stacked meter shows what the plugin scan catalog, the recent-presets history and the session logs actually occupy; deletes confirm in place (the button turns into a red "Confirm delete?" for three seconds — no popup) and settle with a toast, and opening the storage folder or the logs is a row like everything else.

An About panel that answers — the update card has four honest faces: up to date (with the last-checked time), a spinner while checking, an accent card with the new version and a Download button when a release is out, and an error face with retry. The version line copies on click with a "Copied" hint, and an earlier-releases timeline lists the published versions straight from GitHub.

Everything remembers where you were — Settings reopens on the last sub-tab you visited, Alt+1…4 switches sub-tabs from the keyboard, tooltips got rounded corners and a shadow, and the scrollbars fade back when you stop scrolling.
